intent: Fully refactor the existing corporate RAG frontend into a central conversation with evidence opened alongside, separate document and role-appropriate administration areas, and complete actions with durable draft/edit context and local feedback. Empty source selection must search a frozen admission snapshot of all ready accessible own documents; explicit selection must remain strict, retaining existing replay, owner and lifecycle guarantees.

findings.title: Complete the planned protection of unsaved document corrections
findings.suggested_fix: Complete R16 within U4: keep dirty text when a refreshed document disappears, mark the source unavailable and disable saving until explicit discard; bind delayed PDF-mode completions to their originating editor so replacement edits survive. Cover both paths in the browser, then finish U6 acceptance against the final source.
findings.why_it_matters: The explicit plan promises protection of unsaved corrections during status refresh and editor transitions. The frozen implementation adds confirmation for ordinary closes, but still destroys a dirty editor when its document disappears and lets a delayed PDF-mode completion destroy a replacement editor. Those losses existed at the base, so original regression claims #3/#4 are rejected; their continued presence nevertheless leaves the newly agreed R16/U4 deliverable incomplete. No intentional omission is recorded. This is a plan-completeness obligation, not a claim that the refactor introduced those losses.

findings.suggested_fix: Track editors opened during queued/processing independently from accepted correction buffers. When refresh observes ready/failed for that readonly pending view, reopen the current document at its published revision, restoring editing on completion while retaining existing generation and dirty-buffer guards.
findings.title: Reload reopened editors after pending publication completes
findings.why_it_matters: After submitting a correction, close and reopen the document before indexing finishes, or open the old published revision while full PDF reprocessing runs. The document remains ready and is openable, but this branch disables saving and makes every textarea read-only. That new editor has awaitingPublication=false, so Check processing never enters refresh's publication reconciliation branch. After processing succeeds, the dialog continues to show the old text and permanently disabled editing despite explicitly instructing the user to check processing; closing and reopening is required to recover.
findings.validation_reason: Reopening a ready document during queued corrections is permitted by backend/app/documents.py:217-222 and :344-347, but new documents.js:145 and :155 create a disabled editor with awaitingPublication=false that refresh():61-67 never reconciles after publication; test_open_during_correction_becomes_editable_after_publication exercises this ordering, and this confirmation is code-only with incidence not independently measured.
